top_choice_rationale: P002 (Buchwald and Hartwig, Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling) is the one slate item whose impact is verifiable in the synthesis literature: three decades of independent use, several ligand generations, routine use in medicinal and process chemistry, a mechanism understood well enough for rational catalyst choice, and two central, independent laureates with a concrete citation. The novelty margin over the 2010 prize is real but answered by the new ligand classes and mechanistic work C-N coupling required. If the committee puts new capability first, P001 is my second choice: Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work make the Crews and Deshaies concept rational chemistry, and its citation covers both PROTAC and glue strands in wording without crediting more than three. P003 ranks below it because crediting Handa for cereblon identification is target identification for an existing drug, not the design chemistry. No award is last since a mature, well-attributed achievement exists.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no personal, institutional or collaborative tie to any named candidate, but my Masamune-lineage bias toward general synthetic methods favours P002, and my Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr should not be counted as independent confirmation
